sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by stable transfection in BW5147 cells; homodimerization assessed by co-immunoprecipitation/immunoblotting of co-expressed FLAG- and HA-tagged receptor — receptor was surface-expressed and biochemically competent (dimerization assay performed, result: no homodimer detected, but both tagged forms were expressed and detectable at the surface).
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states that FLAG and HA tags were placed 'at the N-terminus' of the full-length, membrane-anchored Fcα/μR. Python computation confirms the signal peptide ends at residue 16 (A) and the mature ectodomain begins at residue 17 (L); insert_after_residue=16 places the tag immediately after SP cleavage, 434 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying all distance constraints. L2 and L3 (same paper) corroborate the same constructs in co-expression and immunoblotting experiments. L4/L5 (PMC8563443) provide additional indirect support via a FLAG-tagged xenopus xlFCAMR ortholog expressed in HEK-293 cells. PMID 23665380: full-length human Fcα/μR stably expressed in BW5147 cells with FLAG or HA tags explicitly placed at the N-terminus; wild-type and cytoplasmic-deletion mutant constructs were used for surface-expression and homodimerization studies. The signal peptide spans residues 1–16 (computed), so an N-terminal tag must be inserted after residue 16 (the SP cleavage site) to remain on the extracellular face; upstream placement would be cleaved off with the signal peptide.

sources.claim: Cells and transfectants BW5147 transfectants stably expressing wild-type Fc α / μ R or mutant Fc α / μ R lacking the cytoplasmic portion from amino acids 481 to 535 ( Δ Cyt.Fc α / μ R), 491 to 535 ( Δ 490.Fc α / μ R), 504 to 535 ( Δ 503.Fc α / μ R) or 524 to 535 ( Δ 523.Fc α / μ R) and tagged with Flag or hemagglutinin (HA) at the N-terminus were established as described previously (Cho et al., 2010; Shibuya et al., 2000).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines converge on a single site: the extracellular N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 16). L1 is the most explicit, naming 'N-terminus' directly for the human receptor; L2 and L3 are the same paper and same constructs used in different assays. L4 and L5 describe a xenopus ortholog (xlFCAMR) with FLAG tag in HEK-293 cells — indirect support for the same terminal position. No ledger line reports an internal loop insertion, a C-terminal extracellular tag, or any other surface-accessible junction; the C-terminus (residues 471–532) is entirely intracellular. The cytoplasmic deletion endpoints named in L1 (residues 481, 491, 504, 524) are intracellular truncation boundaries, not tag-insertion sites, and are recorded in other_positions.
